desc:
A tiny editor starts with an empty text. You are given a list ops; each operation is a pair [type, value]:

  • [1, c]: type the letter number c (1 means 'a', 26 means 'z') at the end of the text;
  • [2, 0]: backspace, delete the last letter. If the text is empty, nothing happens at all;
  • [3, 0]: undo the most recent action (type or effective backspace) that has not been undone yet; nothing happens if there is none;
  • [4, 0]: redo the most recently undone action; nothing happens if there is none.

Typing a letter or an effective backspace creates a new action and wipes the whole redo history (undone actions can no longer be redone). Undo and redo themselves are not actions. Return the final text, which may be empty.

Example: type a, b, c, then undo twice gives 'a'; redo once gives 'ab'; typing d gives 'abd', and a further redo does nothing.
constraints: value is in 1..26 for typing, and 0 for the other types
hints: Storing a copy of the whole text after every action is simple but uses a lot of memory and time for long texts. What small amount of information describes one action?
Keep two stacks: actions that can be undone and actions that can be redone. Each action must remember which letter it typed or deleted.
Undo of a type pops the last letter, undo of a backspace pushes the deleted letter back; redo does the opposite. A new type or effective backspace clears the redo stack.
editorial: Model the editor with the text itself plus two stacks of actions. The done stack holds actions in the order they were applied, and the undone stack holds actions that were undone and may still be redone. An action is stored as its kind together with the letter it concerns, which is all that is needed to reverse or repeat it.

Typing pushes the letter onto the text and onto done, and clears undone. A backspace on non-empty text pops the last letter, records it in done and clears undone; on empty text it is ignored completely, so it must not clear the redo history. Undo moves the top action from done to undone and reverses it on the text; redo moves it back and repeats it. Every operation is O(1), so the total time is O(n).
